findings.issue: Shipping can be refunded early when a FAILED claim is dropped on ship. covered()/uncovered() (Order.java:713) count a FAILED claim as covered, so a sibling cancel frozen afterwards is treated as completing and takes the remainder plus the full shippingAmount. Order.advanceShipment then calls s.dropFailedCancel() and lets the FAILED shipment ship, but the sibling's frozen claim (DONE or REQUESTED) keeps the shipping. Reachable path: seller A cancels S1 and the card reports FAILED (503). Seller B cancels S2: completing, refunded with shipping, DONE. Seller A then ships S1: the customer receives S1 and has had shipping back. The same happens when a whole cancel stops at S2 FAILED with S3 frozen as completing. This breaks AC-7 and moves money wrongly.
findings.fix: FAILED means no money moved (design section 2). So exclude FAILED claims from uncovered() and from the sibling sums in cancelShare/legsFor, and in reclaim() re-freeze share and legs (attempt++) instead of reusing the stale amounts. A smaller alternative: in Order.advanceShipment, refuse the ship with 409 while the shipment holds a FAILED claim and any other shipment holds a claim with cancelShippingRefund > 0 or a remainder share. Add an IT for FAILED S1, then cancel S2, then ship S1.

findings.issue: dropFailedCancel keeps cancelAttempt but does not bump it. If a non-dispatch advance (PLACED to CONFIRMED or PACKED) drops the FAILED claim, the shipment is still cancellable. Its next fresh claim reuses the spent key, which payment-service replays as FAILED, so the first cancel after that returns a spurious 503.
findings.fix: Increment cancelAttempt in dropFailedCancel. Extend failedClaimIsClearedByShip with a later cancel that must use -r<n+1>.

findings.issue: For an uncollected COD order with a wallet part, T3 queues the wallet credit but skips recordRefund (paymentStatus is COD_PENDING), so refundedAmount understates the money returned. The COD payment row and collect amount also stay at total - wallet after a partial cancel. Neither case is tested.
findings.fix: Record the wallet part as refunded and add a COD-plus-wallet case to ShipmentCancelIT. Add a backlog row for adjusting the COD due amount after a partial cancel.

findings.issue: The seller cancel calls seller-service approvedSellerId twice. If the second call fails, the client gets an error after the cancel and refund have committed.
findings.fix: Resolve the seller id once in the controller, pass it into the lifecycle, and reuse it for store.sellerShipment.

findings.issue: AC-3 requires S1's history to be unchanged on 503, but paymentDown_503_unchanged_retrySameKey and paymentFailed_503_retryUsesR1 never assert on order_status_history. The OrderLifecycleServiceTest COD and unpaid cancel cases still build a 4-arg CancelPlan (viaShipments=false), a path paid and COD orders no longer take.
findings.fix: Assert that there is no CANCELLED history row for S1 after each 503. Note in OrderLifecycleServiceTest that those cases cover only PENDING_PAYMENT orders, or switch the COD case to the via-shipments path.

summary: The main mechanism is sound: T1 claim under the order lock, the strict card leg, and an attempt-matched idempotent T3 with the keyed wallet enqueue give exactly one refund, credit, release and event per shipment under concurrency and replays. Changes needed: (1) dropping a FAILED claim on ship invalidates siblings frozen as completing, so shipping can be refunded while a shipment is delivered (AC-7 money error); (2) the line count (stale, see ceo_note); (3) no verify on this SHA. Minors: spent key reuse after a drop, COD-plus-wallet refundedAmount, double seller lookup, AC-3 history not asserted, duplicated INSERT.
